review_notes: Source-first scope: retain the full-sample, full-control outcome regressions in Table 4 Panel A (absolute abnormal accruals), Table 5 Panels A and B (small positive earnings and small earnings increases), and Table 6 Panel A (going-concern report). In each table the selected specification includes INFLUENCE, matching the authors’ stated primary discussion of models with that control. The signed-accrual panels and financially distressed going-concern panel are supplemental partitions. The central next-year bankruptcy accuracy comparison uses a chi-square test after categorizing offices as small/large, so it is recorded as checked but is not a regression model.

The supplied verified reading derivative includes coordinator-verified transcriptions of the performance-adjusted Jones fit, the generic accrual equation, probit Equations (3)–(4), the Altman bankruptcy score, and the footnote-5 Z-score formula. I used those transcriptions and visually checked physical pages 7–9, 12–13, and 19–26. The equation renderer found no embedded equation images on pages 7–9; the relevant vector-text formulas were rendered and inspected directly.

Unresolved details: the source names TA as total accruals but does not state how TA itself is calculated; the clustered robust errors in the probit models are not assigned to a stated clustering dimension; Table 6’s note calls GCREPORT the independent variable even though Equation (4), the table title, and the surrounding text treat it as the dependent variable.
results_review_notes: Extraction is limited to the four frozen full-sample baseline result sets and the related office-fee/client-variable descriptives. Table 4 Panels B and C, Table 5 without-INFLUENCE columns, Table 6 Panel B, and later sensitivity or accuracy analyses are outside this enrichment.
The Table 5 Panel A lnOFFICE coefficient has a table-reported two-tailed p=.171 and a separate one-tailed p=.085 in the selected-results prose; both are retained with distinct roles.
The source states all models are significant at p < .01; these model-level bounds are stored as auxiliary rows in their selected result sets.
